references.text: God tells Abram that his descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and they will become servants there and be oppressed for four hundred years. This points to how the children of Israel completed what was begun by their ancestors.
The Lord declares that He will fully repay both the sins of the ancestors and those of their descendants, reflecting the idea of completing the measure of the fathers' sins.
Ezekiel mentions that children will suffer for the sins of their fathers, which reflects the concept of finishing what the fathers started.

Jesus condemns the scribes and Pharisees for their hypocrisy and says they are witnesses against themselves that they are children of those who killed the prophets, and He predicts that they will complete the measure of their fathers' blood.
